errors.description: The final remark is false as written: for a prime absent from every initial number, any positive exponent divides all zero valuations, so unrestricted exponential divisibility has no unique maximal integer; exponent zero also does not ordinarily divide zero.
errors.quote: the unique maximal $d$ with $v_p(d) \mid v_p(a_i)$ for all $p$ and all $i$.

errors.description: The Type A bound invokes $P_{\mathrm{final}}$ before termination has been established. Apply the same inequality to every finite prefix instead; this immediately rules out infinitely many Type A moves.
errors.quote:
if the play contained $t$ type A moves then
$1 \le P_{\mathrm{final}} \le P_0 / 2^{t}$

parsed.notes: The core proof of both parts is correct. The product/ones potential proves termination after a minor wording repair, and the prime-wise valuation gcd invariant uniquely determines the terminal value.
